newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas trades in Q1 as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas trades in Q1 as prices rise.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures got off to a brighter start to the week with 45 lots traded on Monday afternoon in three separate deals.
This compares with no trade done at all last Monday, and only 55 lots over the whole of last week.

Trade was done in January at 17.90 pence a therm (15 lots, up 0.23 pence from Friday's settlement), in February at 17.90 pence (25 lots, up 0.20 pence) and in March at 14.90 pence (5 lots, up 0.03 pence). The average for the quarter was 16.90 pence a therm.
Encouragingly for the exchange, bids and offers were posted for each of the 12 contract months, and the gap between them was narrower than in the morning.

By the close, front month June saw a spread of only 0.15 pence a therm, between 11.05 pence and 11.20 pence. During the morning session bids and offers were further apart, and by the close of the morning session only four bids were seen.
Open interest remains relatively high at well over 3000 lots, even though recent trade volumes have been disappointing.
